I couldn't open the PR, and the commitlint CI job isn't on the branch. The token isn't allowed to create pull requests (`GitHub Actions is not permitted to create or approve pull requests`) or to push workflow files (`refusing to allow a GitHub App to create or update workflow .github/workflows/ci.yml without workflows permission`). Everything else is pushed to **`feat/38-no-agent-hooks`** and `npm run check` (typecheck, lint, coverage, knip/jscpd) passes. To open the PR: https://github.com/cv/pi-action/pull/new/feat/38-no-agent-hooks

## Commits on the branch
1. **`feat: stop installing git hooks in the target repository`**
   - Removes the "Install pi-agent git hooks" step from `action.yml` and deletes `scripts/install-agent-hooks.js` and `scripts/hooks.test.js`.
   - Keeps `scripts/prepare-commit-msg.js`, because it is this repo's own development hook (run by prek), not the one the action installed. Its tests move to `scripts/prepare-commit-msg.test.js`, so its knip and vitest entries stay.
   - **Test of `action.yml`** (`src/entrypoints.test.ts`): its steps run only `src/index.ts` and `src/push.ts`, and nothing in its `runs:` section mentions hooks, `core.hooksPath` or `--git-path`.
   - **Test of a run** (`src/run.test.ts`): the checkout has `core.hooksPath=.githooks` and pi commits `release: v0.35.1` (the cv/pit#353 case). After the run, `.git/hooks` is unchanged, no `.githooks/` exists, the working tree is clean, and the commit message has no `Refs #…` added.
2. **`docs: say that pi follows the repository's own commit conventions`**
   - Changes the README feature bullet and docs table, `docs/how-it-works.md` and CONTRIBUTING, and adds a "Commit conventions" section.
   - The hook docs were in `docs/how-it-works.md`, not in a README "How It Works" step 4, and the CONTRIBUTING bullet around line 167 wasn't there, so I edited the places that actually described the hooks.
3. **`docs: add AGENTS.md that points agents to the commit conventions`**: a short file that points to CONTRIBUTING. The docs link test now covers it.

## Needs you: the CI commit
Save this as `ci.patch`, then run `git am ci.patch && git push` on the branch. It adds a `commitlint` job to `ci.yml` (pull requests only) that checks every commit between the PR's base and head with the existing `commitlint.config.js`. It also adds the matching lines to AGENTS.md and CONTRIBUTING. It removes `@commitlint/cli` from knip's `ignoreDependencies`, because once the job uses it, knip's hint check fails the build.

With the patch applied, `npm run check` passes. I ran commitlint locally over the same range the job checks: this branch's commits pass with 0 problems and 0 warnings, and adding a `release: v0.35.1` commit makes it fail (exit 1, `type-enum`).

```diff
diff --git a/.github/workflows/ci.yml b/.github/workflows/ci.yml
--- a/.github/workflows/ci.yml
+++ b/.github/workflows/ci.yml
@@ -23,3 +23,28 @@ jobs:
 
       - name: Run quality checks
         run: npm run check
+
+  commitlint:
+    # Every commit of a pull request follows commitlint.config.js, whoever made it (pi included). Hooks can be
+    # skipped with --no-verify; this check cannot.
+    if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
+        with:
+          fetch-depth: 0
+
+      - name: Setup Node.js
+        uses: actions/setup-node@v6
+        with:
+          node-version: '24'
+          cache: 'npm'
+
+      - name: Install dependencies
+        run: npm ci --ignore-scripts
+
+      - name: Check commit messages
+        env:
+          BASE_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
+          HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
+        run: npx --no -- commitlint --from "$BASE_SHA" --to "$HEAD_SHA" --verbose
diff --git a/AGENTS.md b/AGENTS.md
--- a/AGENTS.md
+++ b/AGENTS.md
@@ -2,6 +2,6 @@
 
 Read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) before you change this repository. In particular:
 
-- **Commits.** Use Conventional Commits, as in [Commit messages](CONTRIBUTING.md#commit-messages). [`commitlint.config.js`](commitlint.config.js) has the rules.
+- **Commits.** Use Conventional Commits, as in [Commit messages](CONTRIBUTING.md#commit-messages). The `commitlint` job in [`ci.yml`](.github/workflows/ci.yml) checks every commit of a pull request with [`commitlint.config.js`](commitlint.config.js). `git commit --no-verify` does not skip it.
 - **Checks.** Run `npm run check` before you push. CI runs the same command.
 - **Docs.** Update the documentation when you change behavior. Follow the [documentation style](CONTRIBUTING.md#documentation-style).
diff --git a/CONTRIBUTING.md b/CONTRIBUTING.md
--- a/CONTRIBUTING.md
+++ b/CONTRIBUTING.md
@@ -143,7 +143,7 @@
 
 | Workflow | What it does |
 |----------|--------------|
-| [`ci.yml`](.github/workflows/ci.yml) | Runs `npm run check` on pushes and pull requests to `main` |
+| [`ci.yml`](.github/workflows/ci.yml) | Runs `npm run check` on pushes and pull requests to `main`. On pull requests, the `commitlint` job checks the message of each commit with [`commitlint.config.js`](commitlint.config.js) |
 | [`pi-assistant.yml`](.github/workflows/pi-assistant.yml) | Uses the action of this checkout to answer `@pi` requests in this repository |
diff --git a/knip.json b/knip.json
--- a/knip.json
+++ b/knip.json
@@ -8,6 +8,5 @@
 		"scripts/*.js",
 		"scripts/**/*.test.js"
 	],
-	"project": ["src/**/*.ts", "*.config.{js,ts}"],
-	"ignoreDependencies": ["@commitlint/cli"]
+	"project": ["src/**/*.ts", "*.config.{js,ts}"]
 }
```

If `git am` doesn't accept the shortened patch, apply it with `git apply ci.patch`. Then commit with the message `ci: check the commits of each pull request with commitlint` and push.

## Release notes (proposed)
There is no CHANGELOG file and release notes live on GitHub Releases, so here is the text for the next release:
> **pi-action no longer installs git hooks** (#38). The action used to install a `commit-msg` hook (Conventional Commits only) and a `prepare-commit-msg` hook (`Refs #<first number in the branch name>`) in your checkout. Now pi follows your repository's own conventions: your git hooks, `AGENTS.md` and `CONTRIBUTING.md`. If you want a commit format, enforce it yourself, for example with commitlint in CI, because `--no-verify` skips hooks.

## Open question: version
I chose a **minor** release (2.3.0), and the main commit is `feat:`. No inputs or outputs change; the only difference is that commits the old hook would have rejected now go through. I didn't bump `package.json`, because releases get their own `chore: release` commit.

## Note
Neither pi-action nor pi-durable puts `AGENTS.md` or `CONTRIBUTING.md` into pi's prompt. pi only reads them when it explores the repo, and the docs say exactly that. Adding one line to the built-in requirements block ("follow the repo's AGENTS.md/CONTRIBUTING.md when committing") would make pi follow them more reliably. That changes the prompt, so I left it out.
